extracted.intended_audience: employers, sponsors, agents, and immigration attorneys filing O-1/O-2 and P-1/P-2/P-3 petitions; and USCIS adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and evidentiary requirements for filing, adjudicating, extending, and revoking O-1/O-2 (extraordinary ability/achievement and accompanying support) and P-1/P-2/P-3 (athletes/artists/entertainers) nonimmigrant petitions, including consultation, documentation, validity, and procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: O-2 accompanying alien general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An O-2 accompanying alien provides essential support to an O-1 artist or athlete and may not accompany O-1 aliens in science, business, or education; must obtain own classification but may not work separate from the O-1; must be petitioned in conjunction with the O-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O-2 classification does not entitle independent work; petition must be filed with the O-1 alien's services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary criteria for O-2 accompanying an O-1 artist or athlete
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify the O-2 must be coming to assist in the performance, be an integral part of the actual performance, and have critical skills and experience with the O-1 which are not general and not possessed by a U.S. worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must establish current essentiality, critical skills, and substantial experience performing critical skills and essential support services for the O-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary criteria for O-2 accompanying an O-1 of extraordinary achievement (motion picture/television)
rubrics_metrics.description: O-2 must have skills and experience with the O-1 that are critical based on a pre-existing longstanding working relationship or because significant production will take place inside and outside the U.S. and continuing participation of the O-2 is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For productions, evidence must show significant production outside and inside U.S. and essential continuing participation by the O-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement (general) for O-1/O-2 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with an appropriate U.S. peer group, labor and/or management organization regarding the nature of the work and the alien's qualifications is mandatory before approval of an O-1 or O-2 petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of consultation generally must be a written advisory opinion from a peer group, labor, or management organization with expertise in the specific field and be submitted with the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory opinions must be written and signed by an authorized official, describe the alien's ability/achievements, nature of duties, and whether the position requires an alien of extraordinary ability; if unfavorable must set forth specific facts supporting the conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinions are advisory (not binding) and must be included in the record of every approved O petition except where exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited consultation procedure for arts/entertainment/athletics petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If Service determines petition merits expeditious handling it will contact appropriate labor/management organization if petitioner did not submit an advisory opinion; organization has 24 hours to respond, and must furnish a written opinion within 5 days of request; Service may adjudicate after receiving the response and, if no response within 24 hours, render a decision without opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor/management organization must respond quickly; Service timelines: 24-hour initial response window, 5-day written opinion furnishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding to labor organization when peer group is not a labor organization
rubrics_metrics.description: If petition is accompanied by a written opinion from a peer group that is not a labor organization, the Director will forward petition and documentation to the national office of the appropriate labor organization within 5 days; labor organization then has 15 days to submit written advisory opinion, comment, or letter of no objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will adjudicate petition in no more than 14 days after the 15-day period expires; Director may shorten time for emergencies; if labor organization fails to respond within 15 days, decision rendered without the advisory opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when no appropriate peer/labor group exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If established by the petitioner that an appropriate peer group, including a labor organization, does not exist, the Service shall render a decision on the evidence of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner bears burden to show nonexistence of appropriate consulting entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation content for O-1 extraordinary ability petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with a peer group or expert is required; favorable opinion should describe ability/achievements, duties, and state whether position requires services of an alien of extraordinary ability; unfavorable opinion must state supporting facts; letter of no objection may be submitted if the organization has no objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinion should be specific about duties and necessity for extraordinary ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of consultation for certain O-1 arts re-admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation may be waived by the Director when the alien seeks readmission to perform similar services within 2 years of a previous consultation; Director will forward copy of petition and documentation to national labor office within 5 days of granting waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner should submit prior consultation and advise Director of waiver request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements for O-1 extraordinary achievement (motion picture/television)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult with appropriate union representing occupational peers and a management organization; favorable advisory opinion should describe achievements in motion picture/television and state whether position requires services of an alien of extraordinary achievement; letter of no objection may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinion must address field-specific achievements and necessity of alien's services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirements for O-2 accompanying alien
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with a labor organization with expertise in the skill area is required; for motion picture/television productions, consult with labor and management organizations. Favorable opinions should describe essentiality and working relationship with the O-1 and whether U.S. workers can perform the support services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion should address longstanding working relationship or essential continuing participation for productions with work inside and outside U.S.; letter of no objection is acceptable if organization has no objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service listing of organizations for advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service will list in its Operations Instructions those peer groups, labor organizations, and management organizations that have agreed to provide advisory opinions; the list is not exclusive or exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service and petitioners may use other sources (e.g., publications) to identify appropriate organizations; Service will list occupations/fields where nonexistence of consulting entity has been verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and notification of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall consider all evidence and notify petitioner of approval on Form I-797, Notice of Action; approval notice shall include beneficiary name, classification, and petition's period of validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may consider other evidence as independently required to assist in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording validity periods of approved petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved before services begin, notice shows actual dates requested (not to exceed set limits); if approved after services begin, notice generally shows validity commencing with approval date and ending with date requested (subject to limits); petitions exceeding limits are approved only up to limit specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paragraph (o)(6)(iii) limits and Service policy when setting validity dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity period limits for O petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved O-1 and O-2 petitions shall be valid for a period determined by the Director necessary to accomplish the event or activity, not to exceed 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has discretion to determine necessary period up to statutory 3-year cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: O-3 spouse/dependent classification and employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and unmarried minor children of O-1 or O-2 beneficiaries are entitled to O-3 classification, subject to same period of admission and limitations; neither spouse nor child may accept employment unless granted employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompanying or following-to-join status only; employment requires separate authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of denial and right to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall be notified of the decision, reasons for denial, and the right to appeal under 8 CFR part 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal procedures in 8 CFR part 103 govern substantive and procedural appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: General revocation obligations and Director's revocation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must immediately notify Service of changes in terms/conditions affecting eligibility; amended petition should be filed when petitioner continues to employ beneficiary; Director may revoke a petition at any time, even after validity has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petitioner no longer employs beneficiary, petitioner must send letter explaining changes to Director who approved the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic revocation grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of an unexpired petition is automatically revoked if the petitioner (or named employer in agent-filed petition) goes out of business, files written withdrawal of petition, or notifies Service that beneficiary is no longer employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic revocations are not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation on notice — grounds requiring notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Director shall send notice of intent to revoke if determined that beneficiary is no longer employed in capacity specified; statement of facts in petition was untrue; petitioner violated terms or requirements of petition or section 101(a)(15)(O); or approval violated regulations or involved gross error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must contain detailed grounds and time period for rebuttal; petitioner has 30 days to submit evidence in rebuttal; Director will consider relevant evidence before revocation decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals for denial and revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Denied petitions may be appealed under 8 CFR part 103. Petitions revoked on notice may be appealed under 8 CFR part 103. Automatic revocations may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 8 CFR part 103 timelines and procedures for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission period around petition validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary may be admitted for the petition's validity period, plus up to 10 days before the period begins and 10 days after it ends. Employment is authorized only during the validity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 10-day pre/post windows are solely for arrival/departure personal affairs, not for employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of visa petition validity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must file a request to extend the validity of the original petition on the form prescribed by USCIS to continue or complete the same activities; petition extension generally may be filed only if the original petition's validity has not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate petition extension must be requested when filing extension of stay; both petition and stay dates must match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay procedure and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To extend stay the petitioner shall file application/petition with a statement explaining reasons and must request petition extension; alien beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at time of filing; Director makes separate determinations on petition extension and extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alien leaves U.S. while extension requests pending, petitioner may request Director to cable approval notice to consular office abroad for visa application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension period increments and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized in increments of up to 1 year for O-1 or O-2 beneficiaries to continue/complete same event or activity, plus an additional 10 days to get personal affairs in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are for the same event/activity as original admission; follow maximum increment of 1 year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of extension of stay nonappealable
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial of request for extension of temporary stay may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate motions or refilings may be the only recourse; appeal unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification or preference petition filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of a permanent labor certification or filing of a preference petition shall not be a basis for denying an O-1 petition or related extension/change of status or admission; an alien may pursue permanent residence while temporarily admitted as O-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding or seeking permanent options does not invalidate temporary O-1 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of strikes or labor disputes on petition adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: If Secretary of Labor certifies a strike/work stoppage in the occupation at place of employment and that employment would adversely affect U.S. workers, a petition shall be denied or an approved petition (if beneficiary has not commenced employment) shall be automatically suspended and application for admission denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If strike is not certified by Secretary, Commissioner shall not deny or suspend petition. If alien already employed and participates in strike, participation alone does not constitute failure to maintain status but other terms apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of strike participation by an employed O nonimmigrant
rubrics_metrics.description: An O nonimmigrant participating in a strike is subject to all applicable INA provisions; status and authorized period are not modified by strike participation; participation in strike will not alone be a ground for deportation, but violating status or remaining after authorized stay can lead to deportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in strike does not extend or modify status; alien remains bound by immigration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and retention of Form I-797 approval notice
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS shall notify petitioner on Form I-797 when petition or extension is approved. Beneficiaries not needing a visa may present I-797 at Port-of-Entry to facilitate entry. Beneficiaries needing a visa may use I-797 to apply for new or revalidated visa during petition validity. A copy of I-797 should be retained and presented when reentering to resume same employment with same petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I-797 is an important document for entry, visa processing, and reentry when petition remains valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return transportation liability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an alien admitted under O classification has employment terminated for reasons other than voluntary resignation, the employer whose offer formed basis of status and the petitioner are jointly and severally liable for reasonable cost of return transportation of the alien abroad (to the alien's last place of residence prior to entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when employment terminates involuntarily; defines 'abroad' as last place of residence before U.S. entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: P classification overview and filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 101(a)(15)(P) aliens may be classified P-1 (internationally recognized athletes/entertainment groups), P-2 (reciprocal exchange program performers), P-3 (culturally unique program performers), and P-4 (spouse/child). Employer or sponsor must file a petition for P-1/P-2/P-3 before alien may apply for visa or seek admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (p) sets standards and procedures for these classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 classification description — athlete and entertainment group
rubrics_metrics.description: P-1 applies to aliens coming temporarily to perform at specific athletic competitions at internationally recognized level, or to perform with/ as integral part of an entertainment group internationally recognized as outstanding and who has had a sustained and substantial relationship (ordinarily at least 1 year) and provides functions integral to the group's performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entertainment groups must be recognized internationally for a sustained period; group-member relationships ordinarily at least 1 year.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-2 classification description — reciprocal exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: P-2 applies to aliens coming to perform individually or as part of a group under a reciprocal exchange program between organizations in the U.S. and one or more foreign states providing temporary exchange of artists/entertainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P-2 requires existence of reciprocal exchange agreements negotiated by U.S. labor organization or sponsoring organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-3 classification description — culturally unique
rubrics_metrics.description: P-3 applies to an alien artist or entertainer coming temporarily to perform, teach, or coach under a commercial or noncommercial program that is culturally unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Culturally unique is defined as artistic expression/methodology/medium unique to a particular country, society, ethnicity, religion, tribe, or other group.

rubrics_metrics.name: P petition filing entities and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A P-1 petition may be filed by a U.S. employer, U.S. sponsoring organization, U.S. agent, or a foreign employer through a U.S. agent; P-2 by the U.S. labor organization which negotiated the reciprocal exchange agreement, sponsoring organization, or U.S. employer; P-3 by sponsoring organization or U.S. employer. Petitions may not be filed more than one year before actual need; P petitions adjudicated at Service Center even in emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign employers must use U.S. agents; agents must be authorized to file and accept service of process; agent filing conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to accompany P petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions shall be accompanied by: evidence specified for the classification; copies of written contracts or summary of oral agreement terms; explanation of nature of events or activities with beginning and ending dates and itinerary; and a written consultation from a labor organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear documentation of services, dates, and contractual terms; written consultation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of documentation for P petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, contracts, awards, and similar documentation must reflect nature of achievement and be executed by an officer or responsible person from the institution where work performed. Affidavits by present/former employers or recognized experts must specifically describe recognition and ability/achievement in factual terms and set forth the affiant's expertise and how they acquired the information. Legible copies acceptable; originals may be requested by Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must state facts, not mere conclusions; identify affiant's qualifications and basis for statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itinerary requirement for services in more than one location
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition requiring alien to work in more than one location (e.g., a tour) must include an itinerary with dates and locations of performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itinerary should be detailed and tie performances to employers/venues as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple employer and amended petition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If beneficiary will work for more than one employer within same time period, each employer must file separate petition unless an agent files. Change of employer requires new petition and request to extend stay; alien may not commence employment with new employer until approval. Amended petition required to reflect material changes in terms or beneficiary eligibility; adding additional similar/comparable engagements during validity period may not require amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional P-1 athletes traded between orgs have 30-day automatic continuation with new employer expected to file within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent petitioner conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: United States agent may file for traditionally self-employed workers or when agent arranges short-term employment with numerous employers; agent-employer must specify wage and terms by contractual agreement and provide an itinerary; agents filing for multiple employers must include complete itinerary with names/addresses and may need contracts; burden on agent to explain terms and provide documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent filings subject to conditions; foreign employer through U.S. agent remains responsible for employer sanctions compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign employer responsibilities when using U.S. agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign employer who, through a U.S. agent, files a P petition is responsible for complying with employer sanctions provisions of section 274A of the Act and 8 CFR part 274a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of agent does not relieve foreign employer of statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple beneficiaries, named beneficiaries, and substitution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: More than one beneficiary may be included in a P petition if members of a team/group or providing essential support in same location and occupation; up to 25 named beneficiaries per petition. Petitions must include names and required info at filing. Substitution of beneficiaries allowed for groups by letter requesting substitution and copy of approval notice to consular office or Port-of-Entry; essential support personnel may not be substituted at consular offices or Ports-of-Entry and adding new essential support personnel requires a new petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow substitution procedures carefully; essential support personnel cannot be substituted at ports/consulates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to P petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Key defined terms include: Arts; Competition/event/performance; Contract; Culturally unique; Essential support alien; Group; Internationally recognized; Member of a group; Sponsor; Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify scope: e.g., internationally recognized means high achievement and recognition in more than one country; essential support alien means highly skilled, not readily performed by U.S. worker, with critical knowledge and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: P-1 athlete criteria and evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A P-1 athlete must have an internationally recognized reputation as an international athlete or be member of a foreign team internationally recognized; athlete/team must be coming to participate in an athletic competition with a distinguished reputation that requires athletes with international reputation. Petitions for teams must show team international recognition; petitions for individual athletes must show athlete's international recognition based on reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence should demonstrate reputation and the distinguished nature of the competition or team's international standing.
